docs/pt-br/rust-api.md.previousUtf8:
# API de Rust

Os valores comuns estão disponíveis na raiz do crate: `Project`, `Note`, `NoteType`, `Field`, `Template`, `Content`, `Media`, `BuildOptions` e `BuildOutput`. Os módulos públicos de domínio são `note`, `schema`, `media`, `build`, `update` e `diagnostics`. As ferramentas do repositório formam uma interface separada, habilitada por feature; aplicações consumidoras não precisam delas.

<!-- section: authoring -->
## Criação de conteúdo

| Entrada | Responsabilidade |
| --- | --- |
| `Project::new(namespace)` | Validar um namespace estável de publicação |
| `project.default_deck(name)` | Definir o destino padrão |
| `project.add(key, note)` | Incorporar atomicamente a nota, o modelo e a mídia |
| `project.add_asset(media)` | Incluir um recurso explícito de HTML/CSS/script bruto |
| `Note::basic(front, back)` / `Note::cloze(text)` | Criar uma nota que mantém seu modelo integrado |
| `model.note().field(key, content)` | Criar uma nota personalizada que mantém seu modelo imutável |
| `note.deck(name).tag(tag)` / `.tags(iterable)` | Configurar uma nota antes de adicioná-la |
| `NoteType::builder(key)...build()` | Validar e finalizar um modelo imutável |
| `NoteType::from_bundle(path)` | Carregar um modelo e seus recursos com dados próprios de bundle-v2 |

`Field::new(key).name(display)` e `Template::new(key).name(display)` separam identidade e apresentação. Os templates vinculam chaves de campo, incluindo filtros, seções condicionais e templates do navegador. `Field::required()` verifica conteúdo não vazio; `Field::sort()` seleciona o campo de ordenação. `schema::GenerationRule::all` e `any` recebem chaves de campo. `builder.cloze_field(key)` declara um modelo Cloze.

`schema::FieldKey` e `TemplateKey` são tipos distintos. Strings literais, strings com propriedade, strings emprestadas, `Cow<str>` e chaves emprestadas ou com propriedade podem ser combinadas. As conversões preservam o valor original; a finalização do schema valida as chaves. Uma chave de template não é aceita implicitamente como chave de campo.

<!-- section: content-and-media -->
## Conteúdo e mídia

Todas as strings comuns se tornam `Content::text`. HTML exige `Content::html`. `Content::sequence` combina valores semânticos até a renderização durante a geração. `Media::file(path)` e `Media::bytes(bytes, mime)` mantêm snapshots próprios; suas variantes `with_limits` aplicam um limite `media::MediaLimits { max_bytes }` antes da leitura. O padrão é 256 MiB por recurso. `with_export_name(name)` retorna um valor renomeado que compartilha o mesmo snapshot; clones existentes preservam seus nomes.

`media.image()` e `media.sound()` mantêm as dependências dos recursos. Nomes de arquivo fixos devem ser portáteis e livres de colisões. Recursos explícitos são incluídos mesmo sem uma referência visível estaticamente. Veja [mídia](/docs/media/).

`Note::image_occlusion(media)` retorna `note::ImageOcclusionBuilder`. `.mask(Mask::rect(key, x, y, width, height)).mode(mode).build()` valida as dimensões da imagem decodificada, os retângulos e as chaves estáveis únicas. Tanto `HideAllGuessOne` quanto `HideOneGuessOne` são aceitos. Veja [oclusão de imagem](/docs/image-occlusion/).

<!-- section: build-options -->
## Opções de geração

`project.build(BuildOptions::to(path))` publica um APKG persistente. `BuildOptions::temporary()` retorna uma saída temporária com vida útil controlada. Ambos aceitam `.update_from(previous_apkg)`, `.inspect_limits(limits)` e `.update_policy(policy)`. Uma política sem base de atualização é um erro de configuração. A ordem de chamada dos setters não altera essa regra.

`build::InspectLimits::default()` fornece limites finitos; seus campos públicos podem ser modificados. Todos os valores são `u64`; zero significa zero, não ilimitado.

| Campo | Padrão |
| --- | --- |
| `max_archive_bytes` | 2 GiB |
| `max_entries` | 100.000 |
| `max_central_directory_bytes` | 16 MiB |
| `max_zip_entry_bytes` / `max_zip_total_bytes` | 1 GiB / 4 GiB |
| `max_meta_bytes` / `max_media_map_bytes` | 64 KiB / 16 MiB |
| `max_identity_bytes` | 64 MiB |
| `max_collection_bytes` / `max_media_bytes` | 512 MiB / 256 MiB |
| `max_decoded_total_bytes` / `max_zstd_window_bytes` | 4 GiB / 64 MiB |

Os limites se aplicam de forma independente à inspeção da base e do candidato. Uma verificação que falha informa o recurso, o limite, a quantidade observada e a entrada relacionada, quando disponível. Aumentar um limite é uma ação explícita do chamador; a importação de mídia tem seu próprio limite anterior.

<!-- section: build-compare-and-output -->
## Geração, comparação e saída

`BuildOutput::artifact()` retorna uma referência a um `build::ApkgArtifact` que mantém a propriedade do arquivo. `BuildOutput::report()` retorna observações. Clones de artefatos compartilham a vida útil do arquivo temporário; `persist_to` retorna um proprietário persistente ou `build::PersistError`, com os fatos da publicação e a causa subjacente de E/S.

`project.compare(update::CompareOptions::against(path))` retorna um `ComparisonReport` concluído mesmo se resultados de risco alto bloquearem sua política. Ele oferece `findings()`, `highest_risk()`, `policy()`, `diagnostics()` e `snapshot()`. `UpdatePolicy::default()` bloqueia High/Critical; `.fail_on(level)` altera o limiar e `.allow(RiskCode)` autoriza uma categoria inteira de risco registrada. Ele não pode autorizar evidências de identidade ausentes/corrompidas nem outros erros impeditivos.

<!-- section: reports-and-errors -->
## Relatórios e erros

`BuildReport::snapshot()` retorna `build::json::ReportSnapshot`: observações sem estado de sucesso/falha nem propriedade de arquivos. `BuildOutput::snapshot()` e `BuildError::snapshot()` retornam `build::json::BuildSnapshot`, incluindo o resultado real e o relatório. `update::json::ComparisonSnapshot` separa os resultados originais da análise da avaliação da política. Todos os DTOs de snapshot implementam `serde::Serialize` e não mantêm arquivos. Nenhum trait de extensão é necessário.

Os campos de caminho dos snapshots preservam seus valores nativos `PathBuf` em Rust. Sua forma JSON é uma string para Unicode válido ou uma codificação nativa sem perda: `{"encoding":"unix_bytes","bytes":[...]}` para nomes Unix que não são UTF-8, e `{"encoding":"windows_wide","units":[...]}` para nomes Windows com substitutos UTF-16 sem par. Isso se aplica tanto aos caminhos de artefatos bem-sucedidos quanto aos caminhos de publicação de falhas. Para restaurar um caminho JSON na plataforma original, desserialize-o como `build::json::PathSnapshot` e chame `into_path_buf()`; caminhos codificados de outra plataforma são rejeitados. `PathSnapshot::new(path)` fornece a mesma representação quando você serializa por conta própria o caminho nativo de um erro.

Os erros ficam junto de suas operações: erros de schema e pacote em `schema`, erros de adição/oclusão de imagem em `note`, erros de mídia em `media`, erros de geração/persistência em `build` e erros de comparação/política em `update`. Cada um oferece `kind()` e `code()`, implementa `std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static` e preserva os erros reais de origem.

<!-- section: addition-context -->
## Contexto da adição

Adições que falham deixam o projeto inalterado. O contexto estruturado registra as chaves originais da nota/modelo e o alvo, com detalhes opcionais de conflito ou uso de mídia. Rust oferece `note::{AddContext, AddTarget, AddDetail}` por meio de `AddError::context()` / `detail()`; os SDKs oferecem `AddError.details` com contexto/detalhes tipados. Os campos de Node usam camelCase e são profundamente congelados; Python usa TypedDicts em snake_case. Tags preservam seu índice de inserção; localizações de campo preservam os índices originais da sequência (null/None para o campo, [] para sua raiz) e intervalos opcionais de bytes UTF-8. Erros de baralho padrão na geração não têm chaves de nota/modelo e continuam disponíveis na cadeia de causas.

Imagens tipadas exigem MIME image/* na adição; referências de som aceitam audio/* ou video/*. Outras categorias geram `NOTE.MEDIA_USAGE_INVALID`. Os construtores continuam sem possibilidade de falha; recursos explícitos e HTML bruto não são afetados. A verificação usa o MIME preservado na importação e não certifica a reprodução. A validação independente de MIME/extensão durante a geração continua valendo. Veja o [documento de projeto](https://github.com/morehardy/anki-forge/blob/main/docs/plans/2026-09-28-rust-api-validation-and-errors-design.md) para a tabela completa de alvos/detalhes.

<!-- section: review-once-publish-once -->
## Revise uma vez, publique uma vez

A API de publicação preparada está incluída no pacote público `0.3.1`.

```rust,no_run
use ankiforge::{BuildOptions, Project};
# fn publish(project: &Project) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
let prepared = project.prepare_publication(
    BuildOptions::to("next.apkg").update_from("previous.apkg"),
)?;
let report = prepared.report().clone(); // observations; owns no file
if report.comparison().is_some_and(|c| !c.policy().allows_publication()) {
    drop(prepared); // deletes the unpublished candidate; reprepare with a new policy
    return Ok(());
}
match prepared.publish() { // consumes the owner on every outcome
    Ok(output) => println!("Published {}", output.artifact().path().display()),
    Err(error) => {
        // Replacement may have succeeded even if durability confirmation failed.
        eprintln!("{:?}", error.publications());
        return Err(error.into());
    }
}
# Ok(())
# }
```

A preparação executa a inspeção completa com limites e a comparação. Nenhum destino é publicado até `publish`, que usa o mesmo candidato privado e verifica novamente os aliases da base. # API de Rust

Os valores comuns estão disponíveis na raiz do crate: `Project`, `Note`, `NoteType`, `Field`, `Template`, `Content`, `Media`, `BuildOptions` e `BuildOutput`. Os módulos públicos de domínio são `note`, `schema`, `media`, `build`, `update` e `diagnostics`. As ferramentas do repositório formam uma interface separada, habilitada por feature; aplicações consumidoras não precisam delas.

<!-- section: authoring -->
## Criação de conteúdo

| Entrada | Responsabilidade |
| --- | --- |
| `Project::new(namespace)` | Validar um namespace estável de publicação |
| `project.default_deck(name)` | Definir o destino padrão |
| `project.add(key, note)` | Incorporar atomicamente a nota, o modelo e a mídia |
| `project.add_asset(media)` | Incluir um recurso explícito de HTML/CSS/script bruto |
| `Note::basic(front, back)` / `Note::cloze(text)` | Criar uma nota que mantém seu modelo integrado |
| `model.note().field(key, content)` | Criar uma nota personalizada que mantém seu modelo imutável |
| `note.deck(name).tag(tag)` / `.tags(iterable)` | Configurar uma nota antes de adicioná-la |
| `NoteType::builder(key)...build()` | Validar e finalizar um modelo imutável |
| `NoteType::from_bundle(path)` | Carregar um modelo e seus recursos com dados próprios de bundle-v2 |

`Field::new(key).name(display)` e `Template::new(key).name(display)` separam identidade e apresentação. Os templates vinculam chaves de campo, incluindo filtros, seções condicionais e templates do navegador. `Field::required()` verifica conteúdo não vazio; `Field::sort()` seleciona o campo de ordenação. `schema::GenerationRule::all` e `any` recebem chaves de campo. `builder.cloze_field(key)` declara um modelo Cloze.

`schema::FieldKey` e `TemplateKey` são tipos distintos. Strings literais, strings com propriedade, strings emprestadas, `Cow<str>` e chaves emprestadas ou com propriedade podem ser combinadas. As conversões preservam o valor original; a finalização do schema valida as chaves. Uma chave de template não é aceita implicitamente como chave de campo.

<!-- section: content-and-media -->
## Conteúdo e mídia

Todas as strings comuns se tornam `Content::text`. HTML exige `Content::html`. `Content::sequence` combina valores semânticos até a renderização durante a geração. `Media::file(path)` e `Media::bytes(bytes, mime)` mantêm snapshots próprios; suas variantes `with_limits` aplicam um limite `media::MediaLimits { max_bytes }` antes da leitura. O padrão é 256 MiB por recurso. `with_export_name(name)` retorna um valor renomeado que compartilha o mesmo snapshot; clones existentes preservam seus nomes.

`media.image()` e `media.sound()` mantêm as dependências dos recursos. Nomes de arquivo fixos devem ser portáteis e livres de colisões. Recursos explícitos são incluídos mesmo sem uma referência visível estaticamente. Veja [mídia](/docs/media/).

`Note::image_occlusion(media)` retorna `note::ImageOcclusionBuilder`. `.mask(Mask::rect(key, x, y, width, height)).mode(mode).build()` valida as dimensões da imagem decodificada, os retângulos e as chaves estáveis únicas. Tanto `HideAllGuessOne` quanto `HideOneGuessOne` são aceitos. Veja [oclusão de imagem](/docs/image-occlusion/).

<!-- section: build-options -->
## Opções de geração

`project.build(BuildOptions::to(path))` publica um APKG persistente. `BuildOptions::temporary()` retorna uma saída temporária com vida útil controlada. Ambos aceitam `.update_from(previous_apkg)`, `.inspect_limits(limits)` e `.update_policy(policy)`. Uma política sem base de atualização é um erro de configuração. A ordem de chamada dos setters não altera essa regra.

`build::InspectLimits::default()` fornece limites finitos; seus campos públicos podem ser modificados. Todos os valores são `u64`; zero significa zero, não ilimitado.

| Campo | Padrão |
| --- | --- |
| `max_archive_bytes` | 2 GiB |
| `max_entries` | 100.000 |
| `max_central_directory_bytes` | 16 MiB |
| `max_zip_entry_bytes` / `max_zip_total_bytes` | 1 GiB / 4 GiB |
| `max_meta_bytes` / `max_media_map_bytes` | 64 KiB / 16 MiB |
| `max_identity_bytes` | 64 MiB |
| `max_collection_bytes` / `max_media_bytes` | 512 MiB / 256 MiB |
| `max_decoded_total_bytes` / `max_zstd_window_bytes` | 4 GiB / 64 MiB |

Os limites se aplicam de forma independente à inspeção da base e do candidato. Uma verificação que falha informa o recurso, o limite, a quantidade observada e a entrada relacionada, quando disponível. Aumentar um limite é uma ação explícita do chamador; a importação de mídia tem seu próprio limite anterior.

<!-- section: build-compare-and-output -->
## Geração, comparação e saída

`BuildOutput::artifact()` retorna uma referência a um `build::ApkgArtifact` que mantém a propriedade do arquivo. `BuildOutput::report()` retorna observações. Clones de artefatos compartilham a vida útil do arquivo temporário; `persist_to` retorna um proprietário persistente ou `build::PersistError`, com os fatos da publicação e a causa subjacente de E/S.

`project.compare(update::CompareOptions::against(path))` retorna um `ComparisonReport` concluído mesmo se resultados de risco alto bloquearem sua política. Ele oferece `findings()`, `highest_risk()`, `policy()`, `diagnostics()` e `snapshot()`. `UpdatePolicy::default()` bloqueia High/Critical; `.fail_on(level)` altera o limiar e `.allow(RiskCode)` autoriza uma categoria inteira de risco registrada. Ele não pode autorizar evidências de identidade ausentes/corrompidas nem outros erros impeditivos.

<!-- section: reports-and-errors -->
## Relatórios e erros

`BuildReport::snapshot()` retorna `build::json::ReportSnapshot`: observações sem estado de sucesso/falha nem propriedade de arquivos. `BuildOutput::snapshot()` e `BuildError::snapshot()` retornam `build::json::BuildSnapshot`, incluindo o resultado real e o relatório. `update::json::ComparisonSnapshot` separa os resultados originais da análise da avaliação da política. Todos os DTOs de snapshot implementam `serde::Serialize` e não mantêm arquivos. Nenhum trait de extensão é necessário.

Os campos de caminho dos snapshots preservam seus valores nativos `PathBuf` em Rust. Sua forma JSON é uma string para Unicode válido ou uma codificação nativa sem perda: `{"encoding":"unix_bytes","bytes":[...]}` para nomes Unix que não são UTF-8, e `{"encoding":"windows_wide","units":[...]}` para nomes Windows com substitutos UTF-16 sem par. Isso se aplica tanto aos caminhos de artefatos bem-sucedidos quanto aos caminhos de publicação de falhas. Para restaurar um caminho JSON na plataforma original, desserialize-o como `build::json::PathSnapshot` e chame `into_path_buf()`; caminhos codificados de outra plataforma são rejeitados. `PathSnapshot::new(path)` fornece a mesma representação quando você serializa por conta própria o caminho nativo de um erro.

Os erros ficam junto de suas operações: erros de schema e pacote em `schema`, erros de adição/oclusão de imagem em `note`, erros de mídia em `media`, erros de geração/persistência em `build` e erros de comparação/política em `update`. Cada um oferece `kind()` e `code()`, implementa `std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static` e preserva os erros reais de origem.

<!-- section: addition-context -->
## Contexto da adição

Adições que falham deixam o projeto inalterado. O contexto estruturado registra as chaves originais da nota/modelo e o alvo, com detalhes opcionais de conflito ou uso de mídia. Rust oferece `note::{AddContext, AddTarget, AddDetail}` por meio de `AddError::context()` / `detail()`; os SDKs oferecem `AddError.details` com contexto/detalhes tipados. Os campos de Node usam camelCase e são profundamente congelados; Python usa TypedDicts em snake_case. Tags preservam seu índice de inserção; localizações de campo preservam os índices originais da sequência (null/None para o campo, [] para sua raiz) e intervalos opcionais de bytes UTF-8. Erros de baralho padrão na geração não têm chaves de nota/modelo e continuam disponíveis na cadeia de causas.

Imagens tipadas exigem MIME image/* na adição; referências de som aceitam audio/* ou video/*. Outras categorias geram `NOTE.MEDIA_USAGE_INVALID`. Os construtores continuam sem possibilidade de falha; recursos explícitos e HTML bruto não são afetados. A verificação usa o MIME preservado na importação e não certifica a reprodução. A validação independente de MIME/extensão durante a geração continua valendo. Veja o [documento de projeto](https://github.com/morehardy/anki-forge/blob/main/docs/plans/2026-09-28-rust-api-validation-and-errors-design.md) para a tabela completa de alvos/detalhes.

<!-- section: review-once-publish-once -->
## Revise uma vez, publique uma vez

A API de publicação preparada está incluída no pacote público `0.3.1`.

use ankiforge::{BuildOptions, Project};
# fn publish(project: &Project) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {

)?;

    Err(error) => {

    }

# }

Liberar um proprietário ainda não publicado remove o candidato; a saída temporária publicada segue a regra comum de remoção pelo último proprietário do artefato. Não é possível restaurar um proprietário a partir de JSON nem tentar novamente com um proprietário já consumido. As ferramentas internas de preparação ainda recebem o manifesto completo e sua impressão digital.

Os exemplos usam Rust; Python e Node.js carregam pacotes com `NoteType.from_bundle` e `NoteType.fromBundle` (veja a [API de Python](/docs/python-api/#models-and-templates) e a [API de Node](/docs/node-api/#immutable-models)). Um pacote reúne uma declaração de modelo reutilizável, o texto dos templates, CSS e todas as dependências de mídia explícitas. `NoteType::from_bundle(directory)` valida o pacote completo e captura snapshots dos dados antes de retornar o mesmo `NoteType` imutável usado na criação direta por código. Nomes de exibição como Sentence e Extra são gerados para o Anki após a vinculação. O manifesto é limitado a 256 KiB; cada arquivo de texto de template/CSS é limitado a 2 MiB e deve ser UTF-8. Snapshots de recursos usam o limite padrão de mídia ou um `MediaLimits` fornecido pelo chamador por meio de `NoteType::from_bundle_with_limits`. São verificados tanto os tamanhos antes da leitura quanto os bytes efetivamente lidos. Erros de pacote preservam o tipo/código, o caminho de origem, o deslocamento em bytes quando aplicável e o erro subjacente de schema, E/S, YAML, UTF-8 ou mídia. A finalização do modelo valida o schema; a adição de notas verifica separadamente os conflitos no projeto. docs/pt-br/troubleshooting.md.previousUtf8:
# Solução de problemas

Use os valores estruturados `kind` e `code` da operação que falhou, junto com a cadeia de causas e as observações. As mensagens de texto destinam-se a pessoas e podem mudar. Uma operação que falha e uma comparação concluída cuja política bloqueia a publicação são resultados diferentes.

<!-- section: installation -->
## Instalação

| Sintoma | O que verificar |
| --- | --- |
| Rust rejeita a toolchain | Execute `rustc --version`; use Rust 1.92+ e consulte a versão instalada com `cargo tree -i ankiforge` |
| Node não consegue carregar o pacote nativo | Execute `node -p "process.platform + '/' + process.arch"` e `npm ls ankiforge`; reinstale com `npm install --include=optional ankiforge@0.3.1` |
| Node informa divergência entre o código nativo e o wrapper | Use versões correspondentes dos pacotes; reinstale a mesma versão do registro ou recompile ambos a partir da mesma cópia do repositório |
| Python não consegue carregar a extensão | Execute `python -m pip show ankiforge` e `python -m pip debug --verbose`; confira o interpretador e as tags de sistema operacional e CPU do wheel |
| Python seleciona uma distribuição de código-fonte | Escolha um wheel e um interpretador compatíveis ou siga a [compilação a partir do código-fonte](/docs/development/) com um compilador |

Consulte os [ambientes verificados](/docs/compatibility/), a [instalação de Node](/docs/node-quickstart/) e a [instalação de Python](/docs/python-quickstart/).

<!-- section: models-and-notes -->
## Modelos e notas

| Sintoma | Correção |
| --- | --- |
| Chave inválida ou vazia | Forneça uma chave estável explícita; os nomes de exibição são separados |
| `NOTE.KEY_DUPLICATE` | Atribua uma chave única a cada registro lógico de origem |
| `NOTE.FIELD_UNKNOWN` | Use a chave do campo, não seu nome de exibição |
| `NOTE.FIELD_REQUIRED` | Preencha os campos declarados com `required()` antes de adicionar a nota |
| `NOTE.MODEL_CONFLICT` | Reutilize o mesmo modelo finalizado para uma mesma chave de modelo |
| Erro de referência no modelo de cartão | Use chaves declaradas nas expressões; examine o intervalo de bytes indicado no código-fonte original |
| HTML aparece como texto literal | Use `Content::html` somente para marcação intencional |
| Cartões Cloze ausentes | Use a sintaxe `{{c1::answer}}` com os números permitidos, de 1 a 500 |

Uma falha na adição é atômica. Corrija a nota ou o modelo e tente novamente; não é preciso desfazer um registro parcial de modelos ou mídia. Os construtores de modelos precisam terminar com `.build()` antes de criar notas personalizadas.

<!-- section: media-and-templates -->
## Mídia e templates

| Sintoma | Correção |
| --- | --- |
| Falha ao importar um arquivo | Confira a origem no momento de `Media::file`; a remoção posterior do arquivo de origem é permitida |
| Tipo MIME não corresponde ao conteúdo | Informe o tipo MIME real ao construtor que recebe bytes |
| Conflito de nomes de exportação | Escolha nomes únicos e portáveis; variantes de maiúsculas/minúsculas e de normalização Unicode entram em conflito |
| Recurso de HTML, CSS ou script ausente | Declare-o com `asset` no modelo ou `add_asset` no projeto |
| Importação de mídia excede um limite | Aumente explicitamente `MediaLimits.max_bytes` antes de importar |
| Inspeção da geração excede um limite | Ajuste o contador correspondente de `InspectLimits` para a operação |
| Falha ao carregar um pacote de templates | Use bundle-v2, chaves explícitas, templates baseados em chaves e caminhos internos ao pacote |
| Falha em um retângulo de oclusão | Confira as dimensões de exibição decodificadas, coordenadas finitas e chaves únicas para as máscaras |

Os padrões de tratamento de texto são uniformes em todos os tipos de nota. Nós de mídia coletam suas dependências; escrever um nome de arquivo manualmente não importa seus bytes. Mesmo um pacote válido exige testes de reprodução no cliente para o codec ou a fonte que você pretende usar.

<!-- section: updates-and-outputs -->
## Atualizações e arquivos de saída

Use como base um APKG original distribuído com evidências completas de identidade. Pacotes reexportados pelo Anki não preservam essas evidências. Uma divergência de namespace ou evidências corrompidas não podem ser aceitas por uma política de atualização.

Uma comparação concluída pode retornar `allows_publication == false`. Examine os resultados originais e as evidências antes de permitir explicitamente uma categoria de risco. Não permita todos os resultados indiscriminadamente. A mesma política deve ser passada à geração da atualização se você quiser a mesma decisão. Informar uma política em uma operação que apenas cria um pacote é um erro.

Se um caminho temporário desaparecer, mantenha vivo o objeto de saída ou artefato que controla esse arquivo até que todos os leitores terminem. Relatórios e representações JSON não mantêm a propriedade do arquivo. Em falhas de persistência, examine a etapa de publicação e a durabilidade informadas pelo erro: um erro pode ser retornado depois de o destino já ter sido publicado. Consulte as [garantias dos arquivos de saída](/docs/build-guarantees/).

docs/python/api.md.previousUtf8:
# Python API

The SDK calls the default Rust public API through a native extension. It includes `py.typed` and checked public signatures. Start with the [quickstart](quick-start.md).

## Project and note values

| Entry | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Project(namespace, *, default_deck=None)` | Validates the explicit stable namespace and configures the default deck |
| `project.add(key, note)` | Atomically collects the note, model and owned media; duplicate note keys fail |
| `project.add_asset(media)` | Includes an explicit raw HTML/CSS/script dependency |
| `len(project)` | Number of successfully added notes |
| `Note.basic(front, back)` | Built-in Basic model; strings mean Text |
| `Note.cloze(text)` | Built-in Cloze model; strings mean Text and retain cloze syntax |
| `note.field(key, content)` | Returns a new note with the field assignment; key validation occurs on add |
| `note.deck(name)` / `.tag(tag)` / `.tags(tags)` | Returns a configured note |
| `note.note_type` | The immutable owned model |

Ordinary strings become Text. `Content.text(value)` and `Content.html(value)` are explicit constructors; `Content.sequence(iterable)` composes strings and content without rendering or losing media dependencies. A field does not accept a raw filename as a media reference.

## Models and templates

`NoteType.builder(key)` returns an immutable builder. Its `.name`, `.field`, `.template`, `.css`, `.cloze_field` and `.asset` methods return updated builders. `.build()` validates the complete definition and returns an immutable NoteType. `model.note()` creates a note owning that model. `NoteType.from_bundle(path, limits=MediaLimits())` loads the same model and its assets from the current bundle format; the optional budget applies separately to each asset before reading.

`Field(key, name=None, required=False, sort=False)` separates the stable key from the display name. `Template(key, front, back, name=None, browser_front=None, browser_back=None, target_deck=None, generation=GenerationRule())` uses field keys in every source string. `GenerationRule.all(keys)` and `.any(keys)` configure card generation. The default infers Anki's field-presence condition. A builder's `.cloze_field(key)` declares custom cloze generation.

## Media and occlusion

| Entry | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Media.file(path, *, limits=MediaLimits())` | Reads an owned snapshot immediately |
| `Media.bytes(data, media_type, *, limits=MediaLimits())` | Owns bytes with an explicit MIME type |
| `media.with_export_name(name)` | Returns a new filename value sharing the snapshot; previous references retain their names |
| `media.filename`, `media.media_type`, `len(media)` | Read-only snapshot metadata |
| `media.image()` / `.sound()` | Typed content that retains the snapshot |

`MediaLimits(max_bytes=256 << 20)` controls each import before snapshot creation. Large media can spill to owned temporary storage. Naming conflicts are validated across all explicit and automatically collected assets.

`Note.image_occlusion(media)` returns an ImageOcclusionBuilder. Chain `.mask(Mask.rect(key, x, y, width, height))`, optionally `.mode(OcclusionMode.HIDE_ONE_GUESS_ONE)`, then `.build()`. The default mode is `HIDE_ALL_GUESS_ONE`. Completion decodes the image and validates stable mask keys and finite in-bounds pixel coordinates. On the returned Note, set `header`, `back_extra` or `comments` normally. The generated `image` and `occlusion` fields cannot be assigned manually.

## Operations and results

| Entry | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `project.build(BuildOptions.to(path))` | BuildOutput with a guaranteed persistent artifact |
| `project.build(BuildOptions.temporary())` | BuildOutput with an owned temporary artifact |
| `options.update_from(path)` | Returns options for updating from complete baseline evidence |
| `project.compare(CompareOptions.against(path))` | Completed ComparisonReport, including a separate publication policy decision |
| `options.update_policy(policy)` | Applies explicit risk policy to Update/Compare; invalid for Create |
| `options.inspect_limits(limits)` | Applies finite limits independently to baseline and candidate |

BuildOutput has `.artifact`, `.report` and `.snapshot()`. BuildReport exposes `.counts` (BuildCounts with notes/cards/media), `.diagnostics`, `.comparison` and `.snapshot()`. A report has no outcome or file owner. ComparisonReport exposes `.findings`, `.policy`, `.allows_publication` and `.snapshot()`. Snapshots are ordinary JSON-serializable dictionaries and contain no artifact ownership.

ApkgArtifact exposes `.path`, `.persist_to(path)` and `.close()`. Copying it with `copy.copy` retains another owner; a context manager releases that owner on exit. Temporary output disappears when its last owner is released. Persistent paths survive handle cleanup. A failed persist keeps the source handle usable.

# Python API

The SDK calls the default Rust public API through a native extension. It includes `py.typed` and checked public signatures. Start with the [quickstart](quick-start.md).

| Entry | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Project(namespace, *, default_deck=None)` | Validates the explicit stable namespace and configures the default deck |
| `project.add(key, note)` | Atomically collects the note, model and owned media; duplicate note keys fail |
| `project.add_asset(media)` | Includes an explicit raw HTML/CSS/script dependency |
| `len(project)` | Number of successfully added notes |
| `Note.basic(front, back)` | Built-in Basic model; strings mean Text |
| `Note.cloze(text)` | Built-in Cloze model; strings mean Text and retain cloze syntax |
| `note.field(key, content)` | Returns a new note with the field assignment; key validation occurs on add |
| `note.deck(name)` / `.tag(tag)` / `.tags(tags)` | Returns a configured note |
| `note.note_type` | The immutable owned model |

`NoteType.builder(key)` returns an immutable builder. | Entry | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Media.file(path, *, limits=MediaLimits())` | Reads an owned snapshot immediately |
| `Media.bytes(data, media_type, *, limits=MediaLimits())` | Owns bytes with an explicit MIME type |
| `media.with_export_name(name)` | Returns a new filename value sharing the snapshot; previous references retain their names |

# Python diagnostics and update policy

A successful build returns BuildOutput with a guaranteed artifact. A failed build raises BuildError with observations and publication facts. Diagnostics alone never determine success.

```python
import json
from ankiforge import Project, Note, BuildOptions, BuildError

project = Project('course').add('term', Note.basic('Question', 'Answer'))
try:
    output = project.build(BuildOptions.to('course.apkg'))
except BuildError as error:
    print(error.kind, error.code)
    print(json.dumps(error.snapshot(), ensure_ascii=False))
else:
    print(output.artifact.path)
    print(json.dumps(output.report.snapshot(), ensure_ascii=False))
```

Use machine `kind` and `code` for decisions, not message parsing. All public domain exceptions retain source-chain text in `causes` and chain their native exception. `details` carries operation-specific evidence: template source locations, media paths and budget measurements, incomplete comparison observations, or publication facts. An I/O source becomes a chained OSError where available. `source_details` preserves typed nested errors: bundle text-budget causes include `limit` and `observed`, while media causes include their `code`, `path` and `limit_exceeded`.

BuildReport only contains observations. Its snapshot has counts, diagnostics, elapsed time and any completed comparison. Output and BuildError snapshots contain the actual Success/Failure outcome. Failure snapshots distinguish a destination that was never published from one published before a durability failure. JSON paths do not own files or extend temporary artifact lifetimes.

## Compare before publication

```python
from ankiforge import CompareOptions, UpdatePolicy

comparison = project.compare(CompareOptions.against('course-v1.apkg'))
print(comparison.findings)
print(comparison.policy)
```

A completed comparison returns normally even if it discovers High risk. Check `comparison.allows_publication` to see the policy decision. An unreadable baseline, missing complete identity evidence, invalid candidate or exceeded budget raises CompareError; its `.report` contains observations completed before failure.

Default policy blocks High and Critical findings. After reviewing a specific risk category, acceptance is explicit:

```python
policy = UpdatePolicy().allow('RISK.NOTE_REMOVED')
comparison = project.compare(CompareOptions.against('course-v1.apkg').update_policy(policy))
output = project.build(BuildOptions.to('course-v2.apkg')
    .update_from('course-v1.apkg').update_policy(policy))
```

Acceptance covers every finding in the named category. The findings keep their original risk and evidence. Unmatched allowances produce warnings; warnings do not turn successful publication into failure. Unknown codes, missing evidence and other hard errors cannot be accepted. Do not automatically accept every category returned by a comparison.

`update_from` requires the previous original distribution package, including its complete embedded evidence. Anki re-exports do not preserve that evidence. Omitted notes/cards in an APKG do not automatically delete them from a learner's collection. Review structural changes against the intended Anki import settings.

## Budgets and artifact ownership

```python
from ankiforge import InspectLimits

limits = InspectLimits(max_archive_bytes=3 << 30)
options = BuildOptions.to('course-v2.apkg').update_from('course-v1.apkg').inspect_limits(limits)
```

Budgets apply separately to each inspected baseline and candidate. Media import has its own earlier MediaLimits budget. Budget failures preserve resource, limit and observed values under `details['limit_exceeded']`; increase the relevant limit deliberately and retry. For bundles, pass `NoteType.from_bundle(path, limits=MediaLimits(...))` to adjust each asset’s read budget; manifest and template text retain their separate fixed limits. Required inspections cannot be disabled.

Use `BuildOptions.temporary()` when no persistent path is wanted. Retain the output or an artifact handle while consuming the file; `artifact.persist_to(path)` makes a persistent copy. If persistence fails, PersistError details record the target's publication stage and the original handle remains usable.

Snapshot and error-detail paths are strings when valid Unicode. Unix byte names
that Python represents with `surrogateescape` appear in JSON as
`{"encoding": "unix_bytes", "bytes": [...]}`; restore them with
`Path(os.fsdecode(bytes(value["bytes"])))`. Windows names containing unpaired
UTF-16 surrogates use `{"encoding": "windows_wide", "units": [...]}`, with each
array entry holding one original 16-bit code unit. Encoded paths describe their
original platform. Runtime `artifact.path` remains a `pathlib.Path`, and
`BuildOptions.to`, `update_from`, and `CompareOptions.against` preserve native
path values through the binding.

A missing or mismatched native extension raises an import error identifying `BINDING.EXTENSION_UNAVAILABLE` or `BINDING.VERSION_MISMATCH`. Install a matching wheel, or rebuild a source checkout with maturin. Concurrent operations on one Project are rejected; use independent projects for concurrent work.

# Moving from genanki concepts

Still choosing a library? Read [Anki Forge vs genanki](../anki-forge-vs-genanki.md).

AnkiForge uses stable data keys, validated immutable models, owned media snapshots and explicit build/update operations. This is a new authoring model; it does not emulate genanki objects or the removed AnkiForge Deck/lockfile interfaces.

| genanki concept | AnkiForge equivalent |
| --- | --- |
| Model with numeric ID | `NoteType.builder(stable_key)...build()` |
| Field names used as identifiers | Stable Field keys plus separate display names |
| Note carrying field strings | `model.note().field(key, content)` with an owned model |
| Deck as a note container | Project with a default deck; optional note-level `.deck(name)` |
| Package media file paths | Owned `Media.file(path)` values, automatically collected through typed content |
| Package write | `project.build(BuildOptions.to(path))` |
| Default GUID derived from fields, or a custom GUID rule | Explicit stable namespace and note key |

```python
from ankiforge import Project, NoteType, Field, Template, BuildOptions

model = (NoteType.builder('vocabulary').name('Vocabulary')
    .field(Field('word', name='Word', required=True))
    .field(Field('meaning', name='Meaning'))
    .template(Template('recognition', '{{word}}', '{{FrontSide}}<hr>{{meaning}}'))
    .build())
project = Project('vocabulary-course', default_deck='Languages::Vocabulary')
project.add('dictionary:cell', model.note().field('word', 'cell').field('meaning', '细胞'))
project.build(BuildOptions.to('vocabulary.apkg'))
```

Choose keys from persistent business identifiers. Renaming a display name or changing a definition's text must not change those keys. Do not hash current field content unless content-addressed identity is an explicit requirement of your importer. For source data without keys, assign and persist them outside the SDK.

Template expressions use Field keys. Display names can be translated independently, and the library compiles key references into Anki field names. Model completion rejects missing or conflicting declarations before a note can be added. Adding notes collects model dependencies automatically and rejects conflicting definitions under one model key.

Strings are plain text; wrap intentional HTML with `Content.html(...)`. Use `media.image()` / `media.sound()` and `Content.sequence(...)` to compose content. File snapshots survive removal or edits to the original path. Explicitly declare dependencies referenced by raw HTML, CSS or scripts using `.asset(media)` on the model builder or `project.add_asset(media)`.

For later releases, build a new Project with the same namespace and data keys and call `BuildOptions.to(next_path).update_from(previous_original_apkg)`. The original APKG supplies complete identity evidence. This workflow does not recover identity from arbitrary older packages or promise automatic conversion of existing genanki numeric IDs/GUIDs. Treat the first new-model distribution as a deliberate identity boundary unless a separately validated data migration establishes correspondence.

See [quickstart](quick-start.md), [API reference](api.md) and [update policy](diagnostics.md).

# Generate Anki flashcards with Python

Create and activate a virtual environment, then install the [public PyPI package](https://pypi.org/project/ankiforge/):

```sh
python -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install ankiforge==0.3.1
```

On Windows, activate with `.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1`.
Use ordinary CPython 3.11 or later and a matching platform wheel; CPython 3.11–3.14 is covered by recorded release checks; see [verified environments](../compatibility.md).

## Export a deck

Save this as `main.py`:

<!-- source: bindings/python/examples/quickstart.py -->
```python
from ankiforge import Project, Note, BuildOptions

project = Project('spanish', default_deck='Spanish')
project.add('es:hola', Note.basic('hola', 'hello'))
output = project.build(BuildOptions.to('spanish.apkg'))
print(output.artifact.path)
```
<!-- /source -->

```sh
python main.py
```

Open the persistent `spanish.apkg` in Anki. It contains **hola → hello** in **Spanish**.
Keep namespace `spanish` and note key `es:hola` stable for later edits. Exporting does not require Anki to be installed.

# Generate Anki flashcards with Python

Create and activate a virtual environment, then install the [public PyPI package](https://pypi.org/project/ankiforge/):

```sh
python -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install ankiforge==0.3.1
```

On Windows, activate with `.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1`.

## Export a deck

Save this as `main.py`:

```python
from ankiforge import Project, Note, BuildOptions

project = Project('spanish', default_deck='Spanish')
project.add('es:hola', Note.basic('hola', 'hello'))
output = project.build(BuildOptions.to('spanish.apkg'))
print(output.artifact.path)
```
<!-- /source -->

```sh
python main.py
```

# Rust API

Common values are available at the crate root: `Project`, `Note`, `NoteType`,
`Field`, `Template`, `Content`, `Media`, `BuildOptions`, and `BuildOutput`.
The public domain modules are `note`, `schema`, `media`, `build`, `update`, and
`diagnostics`. Repository tools are a separate, feature-gated surface; consumer
applications do not need them.

## Authoring

| Entry | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| `Project::new(namespace)` | Validate a stable publication namespace |
| `project.default_deck(name)` | Set the default destination |
| `project.add(key, note)` | Atomically collect the note, model and media |
| `project.add_asset(media)` | Include an explicit raw HTML/CSS/script asset |
| `Note::basic(front, back)` / `Note::cloze(text)` | Create a note carrying its built-in model |
| `model.note().field(key, content)` | Create a custom note carrying its immutable model |
| `note.deck(name).tag(tag)` / `.tags(iterable)` | Configure a note before adding it |
| `NoteType::builder(key)...build()` | Validate and complete an immutable model |
| `NoteType::from_bundle(path)` | Load a model and its owned assets from bundle-v2 |

`Field::new(key).name(display)` and `Template::new(key).name(display)` separate
identity from presentation. Templates bind field keys, including filters,
conditional sections and browser templates. `Field::required()` checks nonempty
content; `Field::sort()` selects the sort field. `schema::GenerationRule::all`
and `any` consume field keys. `builder.cloze_field(key)` declares a Cloze model.

`schema::FieldKey` and `TemplateKey` are distinct types. String literals, owned
strings, borrowed strings, `Cow<str>`, and borrowed or owned keys are composable.
Conversions preserve the original value; schema completion validates keys.
A template key is not implicitly accepted as a field key.

## Content and media

All ordinary strings become `Content::text`. HTML requires `Content::html`.
`Content::sequence` combines semantic values until rendering at build time.
`Media::file(path)` and `Media::bytes(bytes, mime)` own snapshots; their
`with_limits` variants apply a `media::MediaLimits { max_bytes }` budget before
reading. The default is 256 MiB per asset. `with_export_name(name)` returns a
renamed value sharing the same snapshot; existing clones retain their names.

`media.image()` and `media.sound()` keep resource dependencies. Fixed filenames
must be portable and collision-free. Explicit assets are included even without
a statically visible reference. See [media](media.md).

`Note::image_occlusion(media)` returns `note::ImageOcclusionBuilder`.
`.mask(Mask::rect(key, x, y, width, height)).mode(mode).build()` validates decoded
image dimensions, rectangles and unique stable keys. Both `HideAllGuessOne` and
`HideOneGuessOne` are supported. See [Image Occlusion](image-occlusion.md).

## Build options

`project.build(BuildOptions::to(path))` publishes a persistent APKG.
`BuildOptions::temporary()` returns owned temporary output. Both accept
`.update_from(previous_apkg)`, `.inspect_limits(limits)` and
`.update_policy(policy)`. A policy without a baseline is a configuration error.
Setter order does not affect this rule.

`build::InspectLimits::default()` gives finite budgets; its public fields can be
modified. All values are `u64`; zero means zero, not unlimited.

| Field | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `max_archive_bytes` | 2 GiB |
| `max_entries` | 100,000 |
| `max_central_directory_bytes` | 16 MiB |
| `max_zip_entry_bytes` / `max_zip_total_bytes` | 1 GiB / 4 GiB |
| `max_meta_bytes` / `max_media_map_bytes` | 64 KiB / 16 MiB |
| `max_identity_bytes` | 64 MiB |
| `max_collection_bytes` / `max_media_bytes` | 512 MiB / 256 MiB |
| `max_decoded_total_bytes` / `max_zstd_window_bytes` | 4 GiB / 64 MiB |

Limits apply independently to baseline and candidate inspection. A failed check
reports the resource, limit, observed amount and related entry where available.
Raising a limit is an explicit caller action; media import has its own earlier
budget.

## Build, compare and output

`BuildOutput::artifact()` returns an owned `build::ApkgArtifact` reference.
`BuildOutput::report()` returns observations. Artifact clones share temporary-file
lifetime; `persist_to` returns a persistent owner or `build::PersistError` with
publication facts and the underlying I/O source.

`project.compare(update::CompareOptions::against(path))` returns a completed
`ComparisonReport` even if high-risk findings block its policy. It exposes
`findings()`, `highest_risk()`, `policy()`, `diagnostics()` and `snapshot()`.
`UpdatePolicy::default()` blocks High/Critical; `.fail_on(level)` changes the
threshold and `.allow(RiskCode)` accepts a complete registered risk category.
It cannot accept missing/corrupt identity evidence or other hard errors.

## Reports and errors

`BuildReport::snapshot()` returns `build::json::ReportSnapshot`, observations
without success/failure or file ownership. `BuildOutput::snapshot()` and
`BuildError::snapshot()` return `build::json::BuildSnapshot`, including the actual
outcome and report. `update::json::ComparisonSnapshot` separates original findings
from policy evaluation. All snapshot DTOs implement `serde::Serialize` and own no
files. No extension trait is required.

Snapshot path fields retain their native `PathBuf` values in Rust. Their JSON
form is a string for valid Unicode, or a lossless native encoding:
`{"encoding":"unix_bytes","bytes":[...]}` for non-UTF-8 Unix names, and
`{"encoding":"windows_wide","units":[...]}` for Windows names containing
unpaired UTF-16 surrogates. This applies both to successful artifact paths and
failure publication paths. To restore a JSON path on its original platform,
deserialize it as `build::json::PathSnapshot` and call `into_path_buf()`; encoded
paths from a different platform are rejected. `PathSnapshot::new(path)` provides
the same representation when serializing an error's native path yourself.

Errors live with their operations: schema and bundle errors in `schema`, add/IO
errors in `note`, media errors in `media`, build/persist errors in `build`, and
compare/policy errors in `update`. Each provides `kind()` and `code()`, implements
`std::error::Error + Send + Sync + 'static`, and retains real source errors.

## Addition context

Failed additions leave the project unchanged. Structured context records the
original note/model keys and the target, with optional conflict or media usage
details. Rust exposes `note::{AddContext, AddTarget, AddDetail}` through
`AddError::context()` / `detail()`; SDKs expose `AddError.details` with typed
context/detail. Node fields use camelCase and are deeply frozen; Python uses
snake_case TypedDicts. Tags retain their insertion index; field locations retain
original sequence indices (null/None for the field, [] for its root) and optional
UTF-8 byte ranges. Default-deck errors from build have no note/model keys and
remain available in the source chain.

Typed images require image/* MIME at addition; sound references accept audio/*
or video/*. Other categories raise `NOTE.MEDIA_USAGE_INVALID`. Constructors stay
infallible; explicit assets and raw HTML are unaffected. The check uses retained
import MIME, and does not certify playback. Build's independent MIME/extension
validation still applies. See [the design](plans/2026-09-28-rust-api-validation-and-errors-design.md) for the complete target/detail table.

## Review once, publish once

The prepared publication API is included in the public `0.3.1` package.


```rust,no_run
use ankiforge::{BuildOptions, Project};
# fn publish(project: &Project) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
let prepared = project.prepare_publication(
    BuildOptions::to("next.apkg").update_from("previous.apkg"),
)?;
let report = prepared.report().clone(); // observations; owns no file
if report.comparison().is_some_and(|c| !c.policy().allows_publication()) {
    drop(prepared); // deletes the unpublished candidate; reprepare with a new policy
    return Ok(());
}
match prepared.publish() { // consumes the owner on every outcome
    Ok(output) => println!("Published {}", output.artifact().path().display()),
    Err(error) => {
        // Replacement may have succeeded even if durability confirmation failed.
        eprintln!("{:?}", error.publications());
        return Err(error.into());
    }
}
# Ok(())
# }
```

Preparation performs full bounded inspection and comparison. No destination is
published until `publish`, which uses the same private candidate and rechecks
baseline aliases. Relative paths bind at preparation invocation. Project edits
cannot change the candidate. Report duration excludes time spent reviewing.
Dropping an unpublished owner cleans it; temporary published output follows the
usual last-artifact-owner cleanup rule. There is no restore-from-JSON or retry on
an already consumed owner. Native builds omit the unused staging manifest but
retain embedded identity evidence and media validation. Internal staging tools
still receive their complete manifest and fingerprint.

Inspect `AddError::context()` for note/model keys and `note::AddTarget` for the original location; `detail()` returns `note::AddDetail` for conflicts or incompatible media usage. Match these non-exhaustive enums with `..` on data variants and a fallback arm. A field's `content_path` is `None` for the field, `Some([])` for its root, or sequence indices for a nested node. Separator byte ranges point into the original UTF-8 Text/Html leaf. `Media::image()` and `sound()` remain infallible. Addition requires `image/*` for images and `audio/*` or `video/*` for sound references. Other categories produce `NOTE.MEDIA_USAGE_INVALID`. This checks retained MIME, not decoding or playback. Raw HTML and explicit assets retain their existing behavior. Export renaming does not change MIME: a PNG renamed `wrong.mp3` passes image addition but can still fail build's independent sniffing/extension check with `MEDIA.DECLARED_MIME_MISMATCH`. Tool recipes now require `ankiforge-project-v2` without top-level `name`; v1 is rejected. Contract bundle is 2.1.0; package identity stays `ankiforge-identity-v1`.

# Build SDKs from source

Use this guide for repository development and unreleased changes.
For the published `0.3.1` packages, use the [Rust](installation.md),
[Node](node/quick-start.md) or [Python](python/quick-start.md) installation guide.

Requirements: Git, Rust 1.92.0 with Cargo, and Node.js 22.13+ with npm or
CPython 3.11/3.12 for the corresponding SDK. The checkout pins the Rust toolchain;
install it with `rustup toolchain install 1.92.0` if needed.

## Source builds

To build the current source checkout:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/morehardy/anki-forge.git
cd anki-forge
```

Rust consumers can use `ankiforge = { path = "/absolute/path/to/anki-forge/anki_forge" }`
in their application manifest. Run examples with `cargo run --locked -p ankiforge --example target_api_basic`.

Build the Node addon from this checkout:

```sh
cd bindings/node
npm run setup
npm run build
npm run pack:local
```

Install both actual facade and host-native tarballs printed by `pack:local` into a separate application using
`npm install --offline --ignore-scripts --omit=optional /absolute/path/facade.tgz /absolute/path/native.tgz`.
These are source builds, not registry installations. TypeScript configuration is in the [Node API](node/api.md#typescript).

For Python, activate a CPython 3.11/3.12 virtual environment, install Maturin,
then run from the repository root:

```sh
python -m pip install maturin==1.15.0
maturin develop --manifest-path bindings/python/native/Cargo.toml --locked
```

Ordinary installed wheels need no Cargo at runtime. Do not mix source wrappers with older registry native binaries.

docs/template-bundles.md.previousUtf8: # Template bundles Reuse the same Anki card design across decks: keep a note type's templates, CSS and media in one directory and load it for normal or Cloze cards. The examples use Rust; Python and Node.js load bundles with `NoteType.from_bundle` and `NoteType.fromBundle` (see the [Python API](python/api.md#models-and-templates) and [Node API](node/api.md#immutable-models)). A bundle contains a reusable note type definition, template text, CSS and all explicitly declared media dependencies. `NoteType::from_bundle(directory)` validates the complete bundle and takes owned snapshots before returning the same immutable `NoteType` used by inline authoring. It does not partially modify a project. ## Run the bundled example ```sh cargo run --locked -p ankiforge --example docs_workflow -- target/docs-examples ``` The workflow loads the [custom Cloze fixture](../contracts/fixtures/template-bundle/custom-cloze/anki-template.yaml) and writes `target/docs-examples/template.apkg`. Its template targets **Languages::Cloze**. One note generates two cards. ## Manifest and template references The manifest filename is `anki-template.yaml`. Only the new format is accepted: ```yaml format_version: template-bundle-v2 note_type: key: language-cloze name: Language Cloze cloze_field: text fields: - key: text name: Sentence sort: true required: true - key: extra name: Extra templates: - key: cloze name: Cloze front_file: front.html back_file: back.html browser_front_file: browser-front.html target_deck: Languages::Cloze css_file: style.css ``` `note_type.key`, field keys and template keys are required stable identifiers. `name` is optional and defaults to the corresponding key. `cloze_field` selects a Cloze model; no separate kind declaration is needed. A field without `required: true` may be omitted. Unknown manifest properties are rejected. Every template uses **field keys**, including front, back and browser variants: `{{cloze:text}}`, `{{extra}}`, and conditional sections such as `{{#extra}}`. Display names such as Sentence and Extra are generated for Anki after binding. The loader preserves original file paths and template byte ranges in errors. ## Load and reuse a model ```rust fn bundle(output: &Path, template_directory: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<()> { let model = NoteType::from_bundle(template_directory)?; let mut project = Project::new("docs-languages")?; project.add( "capital", model .note() .field("text", "{{c1::Madrid}} is in {{c2::Spain}}.") .field("extra", "A city and its country."), )?; let built = project.build(BuildOptions::to(output.join("template.apkg")))?; verify(&built, 1, 2, 0)?; Ok(()) } ``` For an independent application, this full example expects the same bundle copied to `fixtures/template-bundle`: ```rust use ankiforge::{BuildOptions, NoteType, Project}; fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> { let model = NoteType::from_bundle("fixtures/template-bundle")?; let mut project = Project::new("bundle-example")?; project.add("capital", model.note() .field("text", "{{c1::Madrid}} is in {{c2::Spain}}.") .field("extra", "A city and its country."))?; let output = project.build(BuildOptions::to("bundle-example.apkg"))?; assert_eq!(output.report().counts().cards, 2); Ok(()) } ``` The returned model is independent of the source directory. It can be shared with another project or used after that directory is removed. A load failure returns no partial model and cleans up its unshared snapshots. ## Assets and budgets Declare every raw template/CSS/script asset explicitly. Each `assets` entry uses a path relative to the bundle and a fixed export name: ```yaml assets: - path: assets/badge.png export_as: badge.png - path: assets/labels.woff export_as: labels.woff ``` Then templates may use `` and CSS may use `url('labels.woff')`. The `css_file` property supplies the CSS source file; assets are not inferred from arbitrary HTML/CSS/JavaScript. Declared assets remain in the APKG even if no static reference is detected. Export names obey the same portable-name and Unicode/case collision rules as [Media](media.md). The complete export name is limited to 255 UTF-8 bytes, including its extension. The JSON Schema checks syntax and character count; `NoteType::from_bundle` also enforces the byte budget, file contents and references before returning a validated model. A successful schema check alone does not guarantee loading. Absolute paths, traversal escapes and symlinks outside the bundle are rejected. The manifest is limited to 256 KiB; each template/CSS text file is limited to 2 MiB and must be UTF-8. Asset snapshots use the default media budget, or a caller-supplied `MediaLimits` through `NoteType::from_bundle_with_limits`. Both preflight lengths and actual bytes read are checked. Bundle errors retain kind/code, source path, byte offset where applicable, and the underlying schema, I/O, YAML, UTF-8 or media error. Model completion validates schema; adding notes separately checks project-level conflicts. See [custom note types](custom-notetypes.md) and [troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md).

# Troubleshooting

Use the structured `kind` and `code` from the failing operation, plus its source
chain and observations. Display text is for humans and may change. A failed
operation and a completed comparison whose policy blocks publication are
different results.

## Installation

| Symptom | Check |
| --- | --- |
| Rust rejects the toolchain | Run `rustc --version`; use Rust 1.92+ and check `cargo tree -i ankiforge` for the installed version |
| Node cannot load its native package | Run `node -p "process.platform + '/' + process.arch"` and `npm ls ankiforge`; reinstall with `npm install --include=optional ankiforge@0.3.1` |
| Node reports a native/wrapper mismatch | Use matching package versions; reinstall from the same registry version, or rebuild both from the same checkout |
| Python cannot load its extension | Run `python -m pip show ankiforge` and `python -m pip debug --verbose`; check interpreter and wheel OS/CPU tags |
| Python selects a source distribution | Choose a matching wheel/interpreter, or follow [source builds](source-builds.md) with a compiler |

See [verified environments](compatibility.md), [Node setup](node/quick-start.md)
and [Python setup](python/quick-start.md).

## Models and notes

| Symptom | Correction |
| --- | --- |
| Invalid or empty key | Supply an explicit stable key; display names are separate |
| `NOTE.KEY_DUPLICATE` | Give each logical source record one unique key |
| `NOTE.FIELD_UNKNOWN` | Assign the field's key, not its display name |
| `NOTE.FIELD_REQUIRED` | Fill fields declared `required()` before adding |
| `NOTE.MODEL_CONFLICT` | Reuse the same completed model for one model key |
| Template reference error | Use declared keys in templates; inspect the original source byte range |
| HTML appears literally | Use `Content::html` only for intentional markup |
| Missing Cloze cards | Supply `{{c1::answer}}` syntax with supported numbers 1–500 |

An add failure is atomic. Correct the note/model and retry; no partial model or
media registration needs to be undone. Model builders must finish with `.build()`
before they can create custom notes.

## Media and templates

| Symptom | Correction |
| --- | --- |
| File import fails | Check the source at `Media::file` time; later source deletion is supported |
| MIME/content mismatch | Pass the actual MIME type to the bytes constructor |
| Export-name conflict | Choose unique portable names; case and Unicode normalization variants conflict |
| Missing raw HTML/CSS/script resource | Declare it with model `asset` or project `add_asset` |
| Media import exceeds a limit | Explicitly raise `MediaLimits.max_bytes` before importing |
| Build inspection exceeds a limit | Adjust the relevant `InspectLimits` counter for this operation |
| Bundle load fails | Use bundle-v2, explicit keys, key-based templates and paths within the bundle |
| IO rectangle fails | Check decoded display dimensions, finite coordinates and unique mask keys |

Text defaults are uniform across all note kinds. Media nodes collect dependencies;
manually writing a filename does not import its bytes. A valid package still
requires client playback checks for the codec/font you intend to use.

## Updates and outputs

Use an original distribution APKG containing complete identity evidence as the
baseline. Anki re-exported packages do not retain that evidence. A namespace
mismatch or corrupt evidence cannot be accepted by an update policy.

A completed comparison can have `allows_publication == false`. Inspect original
findings and evidence before selecting an explicit risk-category allowance.
Do not blanket-allow every result. The same policy must be passed to the actual
update build if you want the same decision. A policy on a create-only request
is an error.

If a temporary path disappeared, retain its output/artifact owner until all
readers finish. Reports and JSON snapshots are not owners. For persistence
failures, inspect the error's publication stage and durability: an error can be
returned after a destination was already published. See
[output guarantees](build-guarantees.md).

docs/zh-cn/ai-anki-cards.md.previousUtf8:
# 用 AI 助手生成 Anki 卡片

让 AI 助手根据笔记起草问题和答案，对照原文审核后，再用 Anki Forge 导出 Anki
`.apkg` 牌组。在这个流程中，Anki Forge 提供开源卡片生成库：AI 助手负责起草
内容或编写脚本，本地 Python、Node.js 或 Rust 程序负责生成卡片。

你可以先[复制编程助手任务说明](/#ai-quickstart)并选择开发语言，也可以按下面的
CSV 流程操作。网站上的任务说明生成器在本地拼接文本，不会调用 AI 模型或上传笔记。

<!-- section: choose-input -->
## 从可以核对的原始材料开始

选择主题明确的短材料，例如自己的课程笔记或词汇表。如果来源是 PDF、扫描件
或课件，先用其他工具提取并核对文字。Anki Forge 通过 API 接收你提供的内容，
不负责 PDF 文本提取或 OCR。

每个问题尽量只考查一个知识点，并保留必要的上下文，让卡片脱离原文后也能独立理解。

<!-- section: draft-cards -->
## 让 AI 起草 CSV 卡片

将下面的示例粘贴给助手。制作自己的牌组时，替换原始材料，并相应调整笔记数量与新笔记 ID：

```text
Turn the source below into exactly three Basic Anki notes.
Use only facts stated in the source. Do not add facts from memory.
Each question must test one fact and be understandable on its own.
Return only UTF-8 CSV with the header id,front,back, with no Markdown fence.
Use the IDs es:hola, es:gracias and es:adios for these three vocabulary items.
Quote any CSV field containing a comma, quote or newline correctly.

Source:
In Spanish, hola means hello, gracias means thank you, and adiós means goodbye.
```

这段提示词要求仅使用原文事实，生成 3 条 Basic 笔记，保留指定 ID，并按 CSV 规则输出。
输出内容应与以下示例等价：

```csv
id,front,back
es:hola,hola,hello
es:gracias,gracias,thank you
es:adios,adiós,goodbye
```

助手可能采用不同的问题表述。请逐行对照原文，修正含糊或缺少依据的答案，再保存为
`cards.csv`。新笔记使用唯一 ID，之后编辑时保持不变；不要让助手为已有牌组重新生成 ID。

<!-- section: export-apkg -->
## 将审核后的卡片导出为 APKG

[用 Python 将 CSV 转为 Anki](csv-to-anki.md)提供完整程序、安装命令和输入示例。
脚本检查 CSV 格式和 ID 唯一性，生成持久保存的包。示例包含 3 张 Basic 卡片，不含媒体。

如果已有 JSON 数据，或需要图片与音频，可使用 [JSON 转 Anki 教程](json-to-anki.md)，
其中提供完整的 Python、Node / TypeScript 和 Rust 程序。应用程序先解析 CSV 或 JSON，
再将笔记传给 Anki Forge。

需要助手编写自定义程序时，复制[编程助手任务说明](/#ai-quickstart)，补充输入字段、
卡片类型和输出文件名。支持加载 Skill 的助手还可以使用
[Anki Forge Skill](../ai-assistants.md)，读取公开 API 参考与任务流程。

<!-- section: check-result -->
## 学习前检查卡片

在 Anki 中打开生成的 APKG，检查卡片数量、问题、答案和排版。CSV 示例应在 Spanish
牌组中生成 3 条笔记和 3 张卡片。成功导出说明包已生成，并不代表 AI 的答案已经核实，
或适合作为学习材料。

填空题可以使用 [Cloze 卡片](cards.md)。图表标注可以使用
[图片遮挡](image-occlusion.md)，由你提供图片和遮挡坐标；它不会自动识别图中的标签。

保留原始分发 APKG，后续版本按[更新流程](updates.md)操作：保持命名空间和笔记 ID，
检查比较结果，并考虑 Anki 导入设置与较新的本地编辑。

选择主题明确的短材料，例如自己的课程笔记或词汇表。如果来源是 PDF、扫描件
或课件，先用其他工具提取并核对文字。Anki Forge 通过 API 接收你提供的内容，
不负责 PDF 文本提取或 OCR。

每个问题尽量只考查一个知识点，并保留必要的上下文，让卡片脱离原文后也能独立理解。

<!-- section: draft-cards -->
## 让 AI 起草 CSV 卡片

将下面的示例粘贴给助手。制作自己的牌组时，替换原始材料，并相应调整笔记数量与新笔记 ID：

```text
Turn the source below into exactly three Basic Anki notes.
Use only facts stated in the source. Do not add facts from memory.
Each question must test one fact and be understandable on its own.
Return only UTF-8 CSV with the header id,front,back, with no Markdown fence.
Use the IDs es:hola, es:gracias and es:adios for these three vocabulary items.
Quote any CSV field containing a comma, quote or newline correctly.

Source:
In Spanish, hola means hello, gracias means thank you, and adiós means goodbye.
```

这段提示词要求仅使用原文事实，生成 3 条 Basic 笔记，保留指定 ID，并按 CSV 规则输出。
输出内容应与以下示例等价：

```csv
id,front,back
es:hola,hola,hello
es:gracias,gracias,thank you
es:adios,adiós,goodbye
```

助手可能采用不同的问题表述。请逐行对照原文，修正含糊或缺少依据的答案，再保存为
`cards.csv`。新笔记使用唯一 ID，之后编辑时保持不变；不要让助手为已有牌组重新生成 ID。

<!-- section: export-apkg -->
## 将审核后的卡片导出为 APKG

[用 Python 将 CSV 转为 Anki](csv-to-anki.md)提供完整程序、安装命令和输入示例。
脚本检查 CSV 格式和 ID 唯一性，生成持久保存的包。示例包含 3 张 Basic 卡片，不含媒体。

如果已有 JSON 数据，或需要图片与音频，可使用 [JSON 转 Anki 教程](json-to-anki.md)，
其中提供完整的 Python、Node / TypeScript 和 Rust 程序。应用程序先解析 CSV 或 JSON，
再将笔记传给 Anki Forge。

需要助手编写自定义程序时，复制[编程助手任务说明](/#ai-quickstart)，补充输入字段、
卡片类型和输出文件名。支持加载 Skill 的助手还可以使用
[Anki Forge Skill](../ai-assistants.md)，读取公开 API 参考与任务流程。

<!-- section: check-result -->
## 学习前检查卡片

在 Anki 中打开生成的 APKG，检查卡片数量、问题、答案和排版。CSV 示例应在 Spanish
牌组中生成 3 条笔记和 3 张卡片。成功导出说明包已生成，并不代表 AI 的答案已经核实，
或适合作为学习材料。

填空题可以使用 [Cloze 卡片](cards.md)。图表标注可以使用
[图片遮挡](image-occlusion.md)，由你提供图片和遮挡坐标；它不会自动识别图中的标签。

保留原始分发 APKG，后续版本按[更新流程](updates.md)操作：保持命名空间和笔记 ID，
检查比较结果，并考虑 Anki 导入设置与较新的本地编辑。

# Anki Forge 与 genanki

如果正在设计可重复的发布流程，需要拥有所有权的媒体、结构化诊断，以及发布更新前的比较与策略检查，可以考虑 Anki Forge。如果已有 genanki 的 Python 脚本、模板和媒体满足需求，迁移成本高于收益，则应保留经过验证的流程。

| 决策点 | Anki Forge | genanki |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 编写语言 | Rust 核心；Rust、Python 和 Node / TypeScript 接口 | Python |
| 共同基础能力 | Basic、Cloze、自定义模板、媒体与离线 APKG 生成 | Basic、Cloze、自定义模板、媒体与离线 APKG 生成 |
| 身份 | 显式命名空间和笔记键；更新需保留原始 APKG | 可配置 GUID 和数字模型/牌组 ID；支持重新导入更新 |
| 发布前 | 比较发现项、风险策略和已检查的预备候选包 | 由自己的脚本和测试定义发布检查 |
| 媒体所有权 | 图片和音频对象持有不可变数据快照，克隆共享存储 | 脚本提供包媒体文件和引用 |
| 编程式图片遮挡 | 通过公开 API 使用带键矩形遮罩 | 按流程评估合适模型或扩展 |
| 运行成本 | 需要原生依赖；使用受支持平台和解释器 | 保留现有 Python 部署可能成本更低 |
| 迁移成本 | 显式验证旧身份映射、模板和导入 | 已正常工作的 genanki 流程无需迁移成本 |

## 同一个小任务

将三个 JSON 问题生成带图片和声音的牌组时，两种库都由 Python 解析 JSON 并编写笔记。genanki 需要选择模型和牌组 ID、设置字段值与 GUID 规则、将媒体文件加入包，再写出 APKG。Anki Forge 需要选择命名空间和持久业务键，将拥有所有权的媒体组合进笔记，构建 v1，再基于原始 v1 APKG 比较和预备 v2，最后发布。[完整 JSON 示例](../json-to-anki.md)提供 Rust、Python 和 TypeScript 实现及运行命令。

## 已有 genanki 牌组

[genanki 支持自定义 GUID](https://github.com/kerrickstaley/genanki#note-guids)、媒体和重新导入更新。不能将稳定身份视为 Anki Forge 独有能力。默认 GUID 规则可能依赖字段；字段会变化时，应有意选择 GUID 规则。

Anki Forge 不会自动恢复任意 genanki 数字 ID 或 GUID。没有单独验证的映射时，应将首次 Anki Forge 分发视为身份边界。此比较及成功 APKG 构建均不承诺无损迁移或保留全部复习历史。迁移已有牌组前阅读[迁移指南](../python/genanki-migration.md)。

## 历史性能证据

2026-10-08 的比较在 Apple M1 Pro 上测量 Rust Project API 与 genanki 0.13.1。每组 1,000 条 Basic 笔记时，五个实测 Rust 工作负载的导出耗时低 45.7–53.9%；部分媒体场景的峰值内存更高。[方法、原始结果与限制](https://github.com/morehardy/anki-forge/blob/bef4aeb653fc875f216614e73d8a617be039b9cf/benchmarks/results/20261008-latest-commit-genanki/report.md)。该实验未测量当前 Python 或 Node 宿主性能，也不保证这些 SDK 或其他工作负载获得相同加速。

Anki Forge 维护者 · 2026-10-25 根据公开 Anki Forge 0.3.1 API、[genanki 文档](https://github.com/kerrickstaley/genanki)和归档测量复核。开始新任务前，查看[运行环境兼容性](../compatibility.md)并[选择开发语言](https://ankiforge.dev/docs/languages/)。

# 构建与输出保证

`Project::build` 只在操作成功后返回 `BuildOutput`，并保证其中有 APKG 产物。失败时返回 `BuildError`，包含结构化 kind/code、观察结果、底层原因和实际发布事实。

## 临时与持久产物

显式选择所有权模型：

| 请求 | 所有权 |
| --- | --- |
| `BuildOptions::to(path)` | 持久目标；句柄清理后仍保留 |
| `BuildOptions::temporary()` | 临时文件；随最后一个产物所有者删除 |
| `artifact.persist_to(path)` | 新的持久所有者；原所有者仍可使用 |

读取临时路径时，保持 `BuildOutput` 或克隆的产物存活。报告或 JSON 快照不会延长文件寿命。Rust 正常释放所有者；Node 提供 `artifact.close()` 以确定性释放。把路径复制到应用状态中不会创建所有者。

Rust 产物句柄保留绝对路径，即使构建或 `persist_to` 使用相对目标。之后改变进程工作目录不会重定向从已有句柄进行的读取或复制。每个新 `persist_to` 目标均相对于调用时的目录解析。

`BuildReport::snapshot()` 只有观察结果。`BuildOutput::snapshot()` 和 `BuildError::snapshot()` 还说明真实结果。成功快照中也可能有警告。不要从诊断严重程度、路径是否存在或报告是否包含比较发现项来推断结果。

## 基线与发布

更新时保留之前的原始分发 APKG 作为不可变基线，并选择独立输出目标。发布前检查基线证据和候选内容。策略拒绝不会替换输出。缺失或损坏的证据、检查预算耗尽均为硬失败。

发布通过原子替换 APKG 完成。这是单文件保证；写入应用自己的独立 JSON 报告属于另一次操作。普通构建不写额外身份文件：完整的带版本证据嵌入分发包。

发布后仍可能发生晚期错误，例如确认持久性时出错。因此错误快照记录 `PublicationSnapshot` 事实：`path`、`stage`（`not_published` 或 `published`）、`temporary`，以及持久性（`confirmed` 或 `unconfirmed`）。重试或声称没有写入文件前，应检查这些事实。`PersistError` 同样保留发布事实和实际 I/O 源。仅原子替换并不能证明崩溃后的持久性。

快照序列化保留原生路径，不访问文件系统。Unicode 路径仍为 JSON 字符串。非 UTF-8 Unix 路径使用 `{"encoding":"unix_bytes","bytes":[...]}`；含未配对 UTF-16 代理项的 Windows 路径使用 `{"encoding":"windows_wide","units":[...]}`。数组保存精确的原生字节或代码单元。成功产物路径、失败发布路径和绑定错误路径详情均使用此表示。它们描述路径，但不保留产物所有权。文件系统可能拒绝特定原生路径，但其发布失败事实仍可序列化。

## 检查限制

有限的归档大小、条目数量、展开大小、解码集合或媒体及 zstd 窗口预算，分别独立应用于基线与候选包。从 `InspectLimits::default()` 开始，确有需要时再有意提高相关限制。零不是无限制。这些计数器并非进程级内存或 CPU 沙箱；媒体导入另有更早执行的单资源预算。

## 并发工作

Rust 构建借用不可变项目状态。拥有所有权的模型和媒体可跨项目共享。Node 绑定在调用 build 或 compare 时捕获项目快照，之后的添加不会改变该请求。保持产物所有者存活，直到全部读取者结束；另一个消费者仍需路径时关闭最后一个临时所有者，是应用的生命周期错误。

包检查不能证明所有客户端行为。请使用目标 Anki 版本和设置测试渲染、播放与更新导入。调度与 schema 更改限制见[更新](../updates.md)。

<!-- section: prepared-publication-from-source -->
## 准备候选包并在审阅后写入目标文件

预备发布已包含在公开 `0.3.1` 包中。

`prepare_publication` 构建、检查并比较一个私有候选包；`publish` 使用同一文件。选项和相对目标在预备阶段绑定。项目编辑不会改变候选包。仅预备不会替换目标；释放或关闭未发布的所有者会移除候选包。

每次发布尝试都会消耗所有者，包括策略或 I/O 失败。重试或改变策略、目标需要重新预备。报告仍可读取，但不拥有文件。Node/Python 提供幂等 `close()`，以及原因是 `closed` 或 `consumed` 的不可用错误；发布开始后关闭不会取消它。耗时不包含等待审阅的时间。成功替换后仍可能发生晚期持久性失败，因此要检查实际发布事实。

完整操作见[示例](../updates.md#build-once-review-then-publish-from-source)，类型化错误和工作线程行为见各语言 API 参考。

Rust 产物句柄保留绝对路径，即使构建或 `persist_to` 使用相对目标。之后改变进程工作目录不会重定向从已有句柄进行的读取或复制。每个新 `persist_to` 目标均相对于调用时的目录解析。

`BuildReport::snapshot()` 只有观察结果。`BuildOutput::snapshot()` 和 `BuildError::snapshot()` 还说明真实结果。成功快照中也可能有警告。不要从诊断严重程度、路径是否存在或报告是否包含比较发现项来推断结果。

## 基线与发布

更新时保留之前的原始分发 APKG 作为不可变基线，并选择独立输出目标。发布前检查基线证据和候选内容。策略拒绝不会替换输出。缺失或损坏的证据、检查预算耗尽均为硬失败。

发布通过原子替换 APKG 完成。这是单文件保证；写入应用自己的独立 JSON 报告属于另一次操作。普通构建不写额外身份文件：完整的带版本证据嵌入分发包。

发布后仍可能发生晚期错误，例如确认持久性时出错。因此错误快照记录 `PublicationSnapshot` 事实：`path`、`stage`（`not_published` 或 `published`）、`temporary`，以及持久性（`confirmed` 或 `unconfirmed`）。重试或声称没有写入文件前，应检查这些事实。`PersistError` 同样保留发布事实和实际 I/O 源。仅原子替换并不能证明崩溃后的持久性。

快照序列化保留原生路径，不访问文件系统。Unicode 路径仍为 JSON 字符串。非 UTF-8 Unix 路径使用 `{"encoding":"unix_bytes","bytes":[...]}`；含未配对 UTF-16 代理项的 Windows 路径使用 `{"encoding":"windows_wide","units":[...]}`。数组保存精确的原生字节或代码单元。成功产物路径、失败发布路径和绑定错误路径详情均使用此表示。它们描述路径，但不保留产物所有权。文件系统可能拒绝特定原生路径，但其发布失败事实仍可序列化。

## 检查限制

有限的归档大小、条目数量、展开大小、解码集合或媒体及 zstd 窗口预算，分别独立应用于基线与候选包。从 `InspectLimits::default()` 开始，确有需要时再有意提高相关限制。零不是无限制。这些计数器并非进程级内存或 CPU 沙箱；媒体导入另有更早执行的单资源预算。

## 并发工作

Rust 构建借用不可变项目状态。拥有所有权的模型和媒体可跨项目共享。Node 绑定在调用 build 或 compare 时捕获项目快照，之后的添加不会改变该请求。保持产物所有者存活，直到全部读取者结束；另一个消费者仍需路径时关闭最后一个临时所有者，是应用的生命周期错误。

包检查不能证明所有客户端行为。请使用目标 Anki 版本和设置测试渲染、播放与更新导入。调度与 schema 更改限制见[更新](../updates.md)。

<!-- section: prepared-publication-from-source -->
## 准备候选包并在审阅后写入目标文件

预备发布已包含在公开 `0.3.1` 包中。

`prepare_publication` 构建、检查并比较一个私有候选包；`publish` 使用同一文件。选项和相对目标在预备阶段绑定。项目编辑不会改变候选包。仅预备不会替换目标；释放或关闭未发布的所有者会移除候选包。

每次发布尝试都会消耗所有者，包括策略或 I/O 失败。重试或改变策略、目标需要重新预备。报告仍可读取，但不拥有文件。Node/Python 提供幂等 `close()`，以及原因是 `closed` 或 `consumed` 的不可用错误；发布开始后关闭不会取消它。耗时不包含等待审阅的时间。成功替换后仍可能发生晚期持久性失败，因此要检查实际发布事实。

完整操作见[示例](../updates.md#build-once-review-then-publish-from-source)，类型化错误和工作线程行为见各语言 API 参考。

# Basic 与 Cloze 卡片

用代码批量生成 Anki 问答（Basic）卡片和 Cloze 填空（挖空）卡片，无需在 Anki 中逐张添加。Basic 笔记有正面和背面。Cloze 笔记针对每个受支持的填空编号生成一张卡片。本例用 Rust 创建两条笔记和三张卡片。Python 和 Node.js 提供相同的 `Note.basic` 与 `Note.cloze` 构造方法，参见 [Python API](../python/api.md#project-and-note-values) 和 [Node API](../node/api.md#project-and-notes)。

在仓库根目录运行：

```sh
cargo run --locked -p ankiforge --example docs_workflow -- target/docs-examples
```

在 Anki 中打开 `target/docs-examples/cards.apkg`。Basic 的问题为 **hola**；两张 Cloze 卡片分别隐藏 **Madrid** 和 **Spain**。

## 编写笔记

此函数摘自[完整可执行程序](../../anki_forge/examples/docs_workflow.rs)。其中的 `verify` 辅助函数检查成功输出的笔记、卡片与媒体数量。

<!-- source: anki_forge/examples/docs_workflow.rs#cards -->
```rust
fn cards(output: &Path) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let mut project = Project::new("docs-spanish")?.default_deck("Spanish");
    project.add("hola", Note::basic("hola", "hello"))?;
    project.add(
        "capital",
        Note::cloze("{{c1::Madrid}} is in {{c2::Spain}}.")
            .field("back_extra", "A city and its country."),
    )?;
    let built = project.build(BuildOptions::to(output.join("cards.apkg")))?;
    verify(&built, 2, 3, 0)?;
    Ok(())
}
```
<!-- /source -->

`Project::new` 的第一个参数是稳定命名空间。每次 `add` 都需要稳定的源记录键。把同一个键用于另一条笔记会失败；库不会根据内容自动分配键。基于之前分发的包构建更新时，在同一键下修改答案仍表示同一条逻辑笔记。

## 文本、字段与卡片身份

Basic 和 Cloze 的字符串均为 Text。有意使用 HTML 时，调用 `Content::html`；Text 内仍会识别 Cloze 填空语法。`back_extra` 是内置 Cloze 附加字段键。文本、HTML、图片与声音都使用同一个 `Note::field` 方法。

使用 `{{c1::answer}}` 或 `{{c1::answer::hint}}`。普通句子不会提供 Cloze 问题。支持的填空编号为 1–500；修改编号可能改变卡片身份。应通过[比较和更新策略](../updates.md)检查此类更改。

接下来可以添加[媒体](../media.md)、[自定义模型](../custom-notetypes.md)或[图片遮挡](../image-occlusion.md)。

# 兼容性

## 公开包与已验证环境

截至 2026-10-13，公开 Rust、npm 和 PyPI 包均为 `0.3.1`。从 [Rust](../installation.md)、[Node / TypeScript](../node/quick-start.md) 或 [Python](../python/quick-start.md) 开始。

| 接口 | 包 | 运行环境与验证 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rust | [ankiforge 0.3.1](https://crates.io/crates/ankiforge) | Rust 1.92.0 与当前稳定版；四个支持平台的打包消费者，以及全新的公开 crates.io 消费者 |
| Node / TypeScript | [ankiforge 0.3.1](https://www.npmjs.com/package/ankiforge) | Node 22.13.0、当前 22、24 和 26；16 项公开 npm 安装、ESM/CJS 和 TypeScript 检查 |
| Python | [ankiforge 0.3.1](https://pypi.org/project/ankiforge/) | 普通 CPython 3.11–3.14；16 项隔离的公开 PyPI wheel 安装检查 |

已发布的原生包覆盖 macOS arm64/x64、Linux x64 GNU/glibc 和 Windows x64。存在安装包并不等于在每台主机上都通过了运行测试。[Node 覆盖记录](../../bindings/node/COVERAGE.md)、[Python 覆盖记录](../../bindings/python/COVERAGE.md)和发布证据列出具体检查。成功的 `0.3.1` 发布运行分别为 [Rust](https://github.com/morehardy/anki-forge/actions/runs/38371221696)、[npm](https://github.com/morehardy/anki-forge/actions/runs/38371222114) 和 [PyPI](https://github.com/morehardy/anki-forge/actions/runs/38371222047)。其他 Python 实现、自由线程解释器与子解释器需要单独验证。浏览器、Electron、Bun、Alpine/musl 以及 ARM64 Linux/Windows 不在现有 Node 验证范围内。

[批量媒体](../media.md#batch-import-from-source)和[预备发布](../updates.md#build-once-review-then-publish-from-source)指南中的能力已包含在公开 `0.3.1` 包中。

## Anki 导入与播放

普通导出不需要安装 Anki。导入、渲染和播放媒体仍取决于目标客户端版本、编解码器和导入设置。2026-10-08 的基准测试通过了 40 项 Anki 导入、内容和代表性渲染检查（每个实现 20 项），并未覆盖所有客户端或 GUI/音频行为。

更新时保留之前的原始分发 APKG。Anki 重新导出的文件不保留所需标识映射与修订信息。包中不再包含某条笔记，并不会将其从学习者的集合中删除。字段或模板变化、排序字段、本地编辑和复习历史需要针对客户端测试。

使用[手动客户端场景](../manual-validation/anki-desktop-v1/TEMPLATE.md)及各 oracle 记录的具体 Anki 版本和设置评估自己的分发。客户端条件与单文件发布行为见[更新](../updates.md)和[构建保证](../build-guarantees.md)。

# 核心概念

## Project 与笔记

一个 `Project` 表示一次具有稳定命名空间的发布。它可以把笔记放入多个 Anki 牌组：`default_deck` 提供默认目标，`Note::deck` 覆盖该目标。牌组是输出的去处，并非另一层内容编写、媒体或构建容器。

`Note` 携带其模型和内容。`project.add(key, note)` 分配必填的稳定源记录键，并原子地收集依赖。重复键、未知字段、模型或媒体冲突会使操作失败，不会留下部分添加的状态。项目命名空间和记录键必须在编辑及源数据重新排序后保持不变。显示名称和文本不是身份键。

## 模型、字段与模板

`NoteType::builder(key)` 收集声明；`.build()` 校验后返回可共享的不可变模型。`model.note()` 创建持有该模型的笔记。内置 Basic、Cloze 和图片遮挡笔记自带模型。

字段和模板有稳定键与可选的显示名称。编写模板时使用字段键，例如 `{{front}}`，即使 Anki 显示名称为 `正面`。模型完成时会校验并编译引用，包括条件区块、过滤器、Cloze 和浏览器模板。赋值也使用键，不会猜测键或回退到显示名称。

## 文本与 HTML

在 Basic、Cloze 和自定义笔记中，普通字符串始终表示 Text。Text 会转义 HTML；`Content::html` 用于有意加入标记。`{{c1::answer}}` 等 Cloze 语法在 Text 中保留，但这不会使嵌入 HTML 自动成为可信标记。`Content::sequence` 把文本、HTML、图片和声音组合成一个字段。

类型化的图片与声音内容会保留媒体依赖直至导出。添加内容前不要把媒体渲染成字符串，除非也为手写的 HTML、CSS 或脚本显式声明了该资源。

## 媒体所有权

`Media` 持有媒体数据的不可变快照，并管理其生命周期；导出文件名由内容确定。只有在预算范围内完成读取与校验后，导入才会成功；之后源文件可以改变或消失。克隆共享存储，可用于多个项目。`with_export_name` 选择固定且可移植的文件名，不会改变已有克隆或内容节点。

类型化引用自动收集媒体。模型或项目上显式声明的资源，即使静态分析无法识别用途，也会被包含。库不会从任意 HTML 或脚本中自动发现文件内容。

## 构建与更新

成功构建返回保证包含 APKG 的输出对象。报告只包含观察结果；快照是 JSON 数据，不拥有文件。临时产物只有在至少一个产物所有者仍存在时才保持有效。

更新使用上一次原始分发 APKG 内嵌的完整证据。独立比较将发现项与发布策略分开。高风险发现项默认阻止更新；硬错误不能被放行。Anki 导入设置、本地编辑和卡片调度仍需客户端验证。参见[更新](../updates.md)和[构建保证](../build-guarantees.md)。

字段和模板有稳定键与可选的显示名称。编写模板时使用字段键，例如 `{{front}}`，即使 Anki 显示名称为 `正面`。模型完成时会校验并编译引用，包括条件区块、过滤器、Cloze 和浏览器模板。赋值也使用键，不会猜测键或回退到显示名称。

## 文本与 HTML

在 Basic、Cloze 和自定义笔记中，普通字符串始终表示 Text。Text 会转义 HTML；`Content::html` 用于有意加入标记。`{{c1::answer}}` 等 Cloze 语法在 Text 中保留，但这不会使嵌入 HTML 自动成为可信标记。`Content::sequence` 把文本、HTML、图片和声音组合成一个字段。

类型化的图片与声音内容会保留媒体依赖直至导出。添加内容前不要把媒体渲染成字符串，除非也为手写的 HTML、CSS 或脚本显式声明了该资源。

## 媒体所有权

`Media` 持有媒体数据的不可变快照，并管理其生命周期；导出文件名由内容确定。只有在预算范围内完成读取与校验后，导入才会成功；之后源文件可以改变或消失。克隆共享存储，可用于多个项目。`with_export_name` 选择固定且可移植的文件名，不会改变已有克隆或内容节点。

类型化引用自动收集媒体。模型或项目上显式声明的资源，即使静态分析无法识别用途，也会被包含。库不会从任意 HTML 或脚本中自动发现文件内容。

## 构建与更新

成功构建返回保证包含 APKG 的输出对象。报告只包含观察结果；快照是 JSON 数据，不拥有文件。临时产物只有在至少一个产物所有者仍存在时才保持有效。

更新使用上一次原始分发 APKG 内嵌的完整证据。独立比较将发现项与发布策略分开。高风险发现项默认阻止更新；硬错误不能被放行。Anki 导入设置、本地编辑和卡片调度仍需客户端验证。参见[更新](../updates.md)和[构建保证](../build-guarantees.md)。
